full_judgment:
The accused petitioner Md Noor Alam Hossain obtained this Rule calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Natore as well as the opposite party Nos. 2-4 to show cause as to why the proceeding in Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 pending in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Natore under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. At the time of issuance of the Rule the accused petitioner obtained an order of stay for all further proceedings of Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 pending as aforesaid. 

 2. The relevant fact to the issuance of the Rule as appears from the revisional application is that the Assistant Judge, Sadar, Natore lodged a complaint case being Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 before the Magistrate, First Class, Natore, against the accused petitioner under sections 463/465/471 of the Penal Code alleging, inter alia, that the accused petitioner created a false and forged bainapatra and filed the same in Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 which was disposed of before the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Natore in order to obtain a decree of Specific Performance of Contract thereby committed offence under sections 463/465/471 of the Penal Code and in pursuance of an application under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the defendants in Title Suit No. 285 of 1983, the complaint has been lodged by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Natore. Thereafter, the learned Magistrate took cognisance against the accused petitioner under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code. Challenging the said proceeding in Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code, the accused petitioner preferred this revisional application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the instant Rule. 

 5. It appears from the materials on record that the accused petitioner Mr Md Nur Alam Hossain instituted Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Natore against the opposite party Nos. 2, 3 and 4 praying for Specific Performance of Contract on the ground that the opposite party No.2 executed a bainapatra on 17-2-1982 in favour of the accused petitioners for transferring .01 decimals of land and he having failed to execute the sale deed, tile accused petitioner filed Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 for specific performance of contract in which the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 filed 2 separate written statements denying the agreement and execution of the same and also the opposite party No.3 claimed that he had purchased the property after 17-2-1982. The specific case of the accused petitioner is that while the impugned bainapatra has been submitted in the civil proceeding and the same is pending before the competent civil Court the initiation of criminal proceeding against the accused petitioners under sections 463/465/471 of the Penal Code in pursuance of an application filed by defendant under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not permitted under the law  and  as such, the proceeding is an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 6. On the above factual background and the grounds taken by the accused petitioner, we have examined the state of affairs in respect of the proceeding and it appears that the accused petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 for Specific Performance of Contract which was dismissed for default on 11-3-1987 against which the accused petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 1987 under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same was allowed restoring the Title Suit No. 285 of l983. But thereafter the said suit was again dismissed for default on 13-9-1988 against which the accused petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1988 praying for restoration of the Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 but the same has been rejected for default on 25-11-1989. Thereafter the defendants of the Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 preferred an application under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Assistant Judge, who allowed the said application and lodged a complaint on 19-8-1990 before the Magistrate, First Class, Natore, Sadar, which was registered as Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 It appears that the accused petitioner filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1990 before the Court of District Judge, Natore and has taken aground in this revisional application that his Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1990 has been allowed by the learned District Judge, and while the Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 was pending in pursuance of the order passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 9 of 1990 .the learned Assistant Judge embarked upon the provision of section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and lodged the aforesaid complaint case. B1Jt from nowhere of the material on record it appears that the learned Assistant Judge while lodging the Criminal. Case No. 379 of 1990 on 19-8-1990 the Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 was pending before the Court of Assistant Judge, Natore, Sadar, rather the available documents in the record show that the said Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 had no existence on 19-8-1990 so as to debar the Assistant Judge, Sadar in lodging any compliant before the Magistrate against a forged document which has been submitted in a civil proceeding as-evidence in order to defraud the court and which has been adjudicated as forged document. 

 (2) A Magistrate to whom a complaint is made under sub-section (1) or section 476A or section 476B shall, notwithstanding anything contained in Chapter XVI, proceed, as far as may be, to deal with the case as if it were, instituted on a police report. 

 (3) Where it is brought to the notice of such Magistrate or of any other Magistrate to whom the case may have been transferred, that an appeal is pending against the decision arrived at in the judicial proceeding out of which the matter has arisen, he may, if he thinks fit, at any stage adjourn the hearing of the case until such appeal is decided." 

 8. It appears that under the provision of section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure any court is empowered to send for appropriate steps against a person who is alleged to have created a forged document and submitted the same in a proceeding as an evidence in order to obtain a legal benefit out of the said forged document. But before embarking upon the provision of section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure it is the precondition of the provision that the proceeding in which the forged document has been filed must have been ended and any application under section 476, Code of Criminal Procedure filed by any party before that Court cannot be considered unless the proceeding in which the said forged document has been filed has ended. Moreover, the order passed under section 476 of the Codes of Criminal Procedure has been made appealable under the provision of section 476B of the Code of Criminal Procedure, In such circumstance it appears that the instant petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is a misconceived one on two distinct counts: one being that since there was no pendency of Title Suit No. 285 of 1983 on 19-8-1990 when the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Natore lodged the Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 before the Magistrate, First Class, Natore, and the other being that the accused petitioner did not avail the provision of appeal against the order passed under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure while admittedly the learned Assistant Judge, Natore lodged the Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 pursuant to an application filed by the defendants under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 In the case of Amjad Howlader vs Habibullah Bhuiyan reported in 6 BCR 193 a Division Bench of this court has already held that no quashment can be allowed under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure when the accused petitioner being aggrieved by an order passed under section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure failed to avail the provision of appeal available under the provision of section 476B. We are in humble agreement with their Lordships on the point as decided. Under the facts and circumstances of the case we do not find any merit in this Rule which is liable to be discharged. 

 9. In the, result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted earlier is hereby vacated. The learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Natore is directed to dispose of the Complaint Case No. 379 of 1990 pending before him preferably within three months from the date of receipt of the judgment.
